outlet.name: Interscalene (scalene) triangle
outlet.where: Anterior scalene in front, middle scalene behind, 1st rib as the floor. Brachial plexus trunks and the subclavian artery pass through; the subclavian vein runs in front of it
outlet.significance: Most common site of brachial plexus compression (neurogenic TOS); also where the subclavian artery is caught in arterial TOS

outlet.name: Costoclavicular space
outlet.where: Clavicle above, 1st rib below, subclavius in front, anterior scalene behind. Brachial plexus, subclavian artery AND subclavian vein all pass through
outlet.significance: Where the subclavian vein is most often compressed (venous TOS); narrowed by an elevated 1st rib or clavicular somatic dysfunction

outlet.name: Subcoracoid (pectoralis minor) space
outlet.where: Coracoid process above, pectoralis minor in front, upper ribs behind. Brachial plexus, axillary artery and axillary vein pass through
outlet.significance: Not strictly part of the thoracic outlet, yet compression here is almost as common as in the scalene triangle; a hypertonic front-wall muscle or rib dysfunction narrows it

outlet.name: Cervical rib
outlet.where: Congenital extra rib arising from C7 that crowds the brachial plexus and subclavian artery where they cross the 1st rib
outlet.significance: Seen on plain neck or chest films; it or an anomalous 1st rib underlies almost every case of arterial TOS

outlet.name: Anterior & middle scalenes
outlet.where: One arises from C3-C6, the other from C2-C7; both run down to insert on the 1st rib
outlet.significance: Hypertonicity or cervical somatic dysfunction narrows the triangle; their trigger points refer pain to the arm, chest and upper back and can mimic TOS

outlet.name: Rib 1 inhalation somatic dysfunction
outlet.where: 1st rib held up and resisting exhalation, raising the floor of the triangle and narrowing the gap under the clavicle
outlet.significance: A compressive cause of TOS symptoms; treated with muscle energy for the elevated 1st rib, with thoracic inlet release and cervical myofascial release

outlet.name: Adson's test
outlet.where: Examiner behind the patient stabilizes the shoulder and clavicle, extends the shoulder and monitors the radial pulse; board versions add neck extension, the head turned toward that side and a deep breath
outlet.significance: The most commonly used TOS test: a fading or absent pulse, or reproduced pain/paresthesia, implicates tight scalenes or an extra rib; false positives and negatives occur, so combine tests

outlet.name: Wright's (hyperabduction) test
outlet.where: The arm is passively raised fully overhead and externally rotated while the radial pulse is monitored
outlet.significance: Pulse loss or reproduced symptoms point to compression beneath the pectoralis minor, below the coracoid

outlet.name: Roos test (elevated arm stress test)
outlet.where: Both arms abducted 90° and externally rotated with the elbows bent 90°; the patient slowly opens and closes the hands for 3 minutes
outlet.significance: Positive if heaviness, pain or numbness forces the arms down early - a general provocative test for TOS

outlet.name: Costoclavicular (military brace) maneuver
outlet.where: The patient pulls the shoulders back and down with the chest pushed out, as if at attention, while the radial pulse is monitored
outlet.significance: Pulse loss or reproduced symptoms point to compression between the clavicle and the 1st rib

outlet.name: Spurling test
outlet.where: The neck is extended and side-bent/rotated toward the painful side, then pressed down from above
outlet.significance: Arm pain shooting down a dermatome points to cervical nerve root impingement - a mimic of (or companion to) TOS that must be excluded

outlet.name: Tinel's sign
outlet.where: Tapping over the ulnar groove at the elbow and over the median nerve at the wrist
outlet.significance: Tingling into the hand suggests a distal entrapment (ulnar at the elbow, carpal tunnel) that can mimic or coexist with TOS

outlet.name: Anterior scalene block
outlet.where: Local anesthetic injected into the front muscle wall of the triangle over the 1st rib (the muscle arising from C3-C6)
outlet.significance: Diagnostic and therapeutic: relief predicts a 94% good outcome after surgery, versus 50% in patients the injection fails to help

outlet.name: Conservative TOS care
outlet.where: Posture, stretching and strengthening rehab, OMT, activity changes and ergonomics, stress reduction, weight control, NSAIDs or muscle relaxants, and injections
outlet.significance: First line when there is no significant neurologic or vascular compromise; give an adequate 4-6 month trial with patient education and monitoring

outlet.name: 1st rib resection with scalenectomy
outlet.where: Surgical removal of the 1st rib, often with cutting or removing the neck muscles that form the triangle's front and back walls
outlet.significance: For neurogenic TOS that fails conservative care (excellent results in ~95%); often the initial management for arterial or venous TOS; risk includes brachial plexus injury
